who: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Opus 5.5), lane: crates/blaze-program, merge-1113, round 3
what: Two oracles of the program simulation were wrong, not the code under test, and two rounds of fixes went at the code: the run oracle printed a static's raw bytes (its relocated field holds an address, so any move of the function it points at made a correct run differ), and the fresh build it compared against was built all at the fast tier, so after any tier-up the node sets could not match. The failure messages said only 'a run differs' and 'N nodes against M', so the cause had to be guessed in a lane that cannot run anything.
cost: two compile-and-test rounds of the main agent spent on fixes aimed at the wrong cause
cause: an oracle that compares a layout quantity (an address) as behaviour, and a reference build that does not take the same state (the tier of each row) as the system under test; failure messages that do not name the node
class: an oracle not derived from the same rule as the code it checks, with failures that do not name the differing thing
prevention: build the reference with the code's own rule (here Program::seeds with Program::top_tier); compare content, never addresses; every oracle failure names the first differing node and how (first_difference)
fix: world.rs: Event::Static carries the static's view; fresh() takes the top-tier set; first_difference names missing/extra row, other key or other bytes
state: fixed, unverified until the main agent runs the tests
